The Auto-Regressive Moving-Average model (ARMA)⁷⁻¹⁰ that can automatically generate control parameters based on previous performance and has shown more robust than a PI controller in a machining process will be used.

The draw-in sensor produces good linear results and insensitivity to pulling speed and starting position. Since material type affects the sensitivity of the transducer, the draw-in sensor’s input voltage is adjustable to obtain the highest maximum output voltage. Although the movement of the blank holder block causes a change in the output voltage, the change does not affect the linearity of the results. With these capabilities, the draw-in sensor is effective and ready to be implemented in the discussed further work. The implementation and integration of the draw-in sensor will make the stamping tool sense the material movement inside the forming press and make intelligent process adjustment to maximize material’s potentials. Furthermore, the lead-time for introducing new light-weight materials into mass production can be dramatically decreased and the consistency of stamping products will be increased.
